clue.text: Nameless wild flower

indicators.note: the word reads as name-less: N, the usual abbreviation for name, is dropped

parts.note: a wild storm or temper is a violent one

explanation.surface: A flower of unknown name found growing in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' is the deletion signal: N (name) leaves VIOLENT. 'wild flower' looks like one phrase, but 'wild' is the wordplay and 'flower' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet is a small purple-flowered plant, so it is one kind of bloom.

clue.text: Living the life of Riley, including a paramour

parts.note: inc. is a short form for including or inclusive
a paramour is a lover

explanation.surface: Enjoying a carefree life, with a mistress in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the life of Riley' is an idiom for a luxurious, carefree existence.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in clover is to live in comfort and prosperity, as cattle in a rich pasture.

clue.text: Apprentice very much within the rules

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
awfully means extremely, very much

explanation.surface: A trainee follows procedure to the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting lawfully means acting legally, in keeping with the law.

clue.text: Prominent (in some small measure) man given warning

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
he is the pronoun for a man
golfers shout fore as a warning

explanation.surface: A fellow becomes somewhat conspicuous after being cautioned.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golfer's warning cry; 'in some' and 'given' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the front, conspicuous or prominent in view.

clue.text: The Australian farmer is more. stocky

definitions.meaning: in Australia a ... was a grazier who took up large tracts of land for stock
comparative of squat, short and thickset

explanation.surface: An Aussie rancher is described as being built more heavily than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian sheep graziers were historically called squatters; and squat means thickset, so its comparative means thicker-set.

clue.text: Procrustes might take some exercise

definitions.meaning: Procrustes, the robber of Greek myth, stretched guests to fit his bed
to go for a short walk after sitting

explanation.surface: The mythical robber may go out for a constitutional.
explanation.walkthrough: Procrustes literally stretched his victims' limbs to fit his bed; the idiom means going for a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for walking to loosen up, and literally describes Procrustes racking limbs.

clue.text: Seaman, a solitary denizen of the sea

parts.note: AB stands for able-bodied seaman
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A lonely sailor dwells by the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible marine mollusc, an ear-shaped sea snail.

clue.text: Repairing a lute? Get some instruction

indicators.note: repairing reworks the letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Fixing a stringed instrument? Take some lessons first.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange A LUTE plus GET. 'some' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is the teaching or guidance given by a tutor.

clue.text: The rest haven't got a clue

indicators.note: the word for the rest lacks the letter given

parts.note: the remainder is what is left

explanation.surface: Everyone else is clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haven't got a clue' reads as a cliché about ignorance, but splits into 'haven't got a' (drop A) and the definition 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue can be a hint that jogs the memory, something that prompts recall.

clue.text: A result of global warming — one we trace with difficulty

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: letters assembled with difficulty are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tracing a consequence of climate change finds the job hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' is the anagram signal. The definition is a whimsical take: melting polar ice gives chilled meltwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Warming melts glaciers and ice caps, producing chilled meltwater as a consequence.

clue.text: Stop army taking on married man who's short but aggressive

parts.note: to ban something is to stop it
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A soldier is barred from taking on a small but pugnacious husband.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time army reserve. 'taking on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small fighting fowl, hence figuratively a small, combative person.

clue.text: Ancient letter cut into minute. headstone

indicators.note: one piece is cut into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a minute can mean a moment, a brief time
nu is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An old inscription is carved into a tiny gravestone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like 'tiny' describing the headstone but is the noun, a brief time.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone is a memorial, and a memorial erected to the dead is a commemorative structure.

clue.text: Almost lose sight of Brownie

indicators.note: almost the whole phrase, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to lose sight is to go blind

explanation.surface: Nearly failing to spot a young Girl Guide.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brownie is a junior Girl Guide, but here it is the household sprite of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a brownie is a small mischievous elf or sprite, much like an impish creature of fairy tales.

clue.text: I agree with man steeped in knowledge — I protest!

indicators.note: the first pieces are steeped in, so placed within, the word for knowledge

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
OK is said to show agreement
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone well-read concurs, then voices an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an indignant exclamation used to object, as in 'Now see here!'

clue.text: This rogue, if reformed, could become law-abiding

indicators.note: the letters, once reformed, take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rascal who mended his ways could go straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright, virtuous and honest.

clue.text: Adult interrupts. young things fighting

indicators.note: the abbreviation breaks into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: fry are young fish
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up breaks up a scrap between youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young things' sounds like children but means fry, newly hatched fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or battle, the thick of the action.

clue.text: Bird making passionate love

parts.note: flaming describes intense, passionate feeling
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bird engages in fiery romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a long-legged pink wading bird.

clue.text: Friendly, even when caught out

parts.note: a word for friendly that stays a word for friendly when C, the cricket abbreviation for caught, is taken out of it

explanation.surface: Someone stays good-natured even when found out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C (caught, from cricket) and AMIABLE remains, still meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means peaceable and well-disposed, characterised by goodwill.

clue.text: Prophet whose errand's obscured

indicators.note: the word lies obscured inside the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A soothsayer's mission is shrouded in mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is one who sees into the future, a prophet or visionary.

clue.text: Clashing of sword handle against spear

indicators.note: the handle of the sword is its first letter, where it is held

parts.note: a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: A swordsman's hilt clangs against a pike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' takes the first letter, the end you hold. 'against' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident sounds are harsh and grating, jarring like clashing noise.

clue.text: Cherish, sinner he can be rehabilitated

indicators.note: the letters can be rehabilitated, reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Value the wrongdoer: he can be reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine is to hold sacred, preserving and treasuring something.

clue.text: Dispatched, almost within a week .

indicators.note: the second word is placed within the first

parts.note: something dispatched has been sent
nigh means nearly

explanation.surface: Sent off, nearly, in under seven days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like it trims a word, but it is a plain synonym. A sennight is an old word for a week, as fortnight is for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Sennight is an archaic word for a period of seven nights and days, as fortnight is fourteen.

clue.text: Have doubts about foul' stroke

indicators.note: the word for doubts goes about, so around, the word for foul

parts.note: to sus is slang for suspect, have doubts about
olid means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: Being suspicious about a dirty punch.
explanation.walkthrough: OLID is a rare word for foul-smelling. The solidus is the slash mark (/).
explanation.definitionFit: A solidus is an oblique printed line, the slash used between words or figures.

clue.text: "Spot the raincoat", you'll say

indicators.note: what you say is heard, so the sound of the words gives the answer

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, followed by you'll

explanation.surface: A quiz-show prompt asking you to identify the waterproof coat.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC (raincoat) plus 'you'll' spoken together sound like the answer. 'Spot the...' is the cliché of picture puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A macule is a blemish or stain on the skin, a flat mark.

clue.text: Wait patiently, it's coming back fast

indicators.note: the shortened form comes back, so it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: 'tis is the poetic contraction of it is
held fast means held tight

explanation.surface: Wait calmly: the thing is returning quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' expands to 'tis, which read backwards gives SIT. 'fast' is not speed but firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put and not act, holding one's position while waiting for things to develop.

clue.text: A person of importance, oddly — oddly, a person of no importance

parts.note: a nob is a person of wealth or high status

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of the preceding word

explanation.surface: A bigwig, oddly enough, turns out to be a nonentity.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'oddly' is the fodder: its odd letters O, D, Y follow NOB. The second 'oddly' is the selector.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonentity: someone who counts for little in society.

clue.text: Arcane coteries broken up

indicators.note: the word is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Secretive cliques have been disbanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood by only a small initiated circle, hence obscure.

clue.text: Foreign love poetry, for instance

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
verse is poetry
as, as in such as

explanation.surface: Romantic verse from abroad, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means abroad, in or from another country.

clue.text: Dolly is a child-minder

definitions.meaning: in cricket a dolly is a very easy catch
someone paid to look after children while the parents are out

explanation.surface: A girl called Dolly works as a nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a dolly is a simple catch to the fielder, also called a sitter. 'Dolly' poses as a name or toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is cricket slang for a simple catch, and also short for a babysitter who looks after children.
